This specific morphological feature supported the malignancy diagnosis over bacterial infection, despite the classifier's bias toward common infectious patterns. The case highlights that while AI classifiers may detect general opacity or pneumonia patterns, specific structural details like pseudocavitation are key to distinguishing pneumonic adenocarcinoma from typical infectious consolidations.", "In a case of a patient with COVID-19 pneumonia experiencing sudden clinical worsening (right hemithorax pain, crackles) 18 days after admission, the correct diagnosis was identified as a right-sided pneumothorax. The source feedback highlights that while automated chest X-ray classifiers returned no strong findings (scores below threshold), this does not imply normality or rule out pathology like pneumothorax. The key learning is to rely on clinical context (sudden pain, worsening) and specific radiological signs (loss of lung volume, visceral pleural line) rather than relying solely on classifier outputs which may miss subtle or acute changes, especially when comparing serial images where chronology must be explicitly established by the question prompt."]
